title: Port ship damage counters, the module 11 repair move (FUN_004c8e90) and the original repair cadence
description: Answered by or-lzz3 (ghidra/notes/ship-damage-repair.md). ship+0x64 packs six 4-bit damage counters (shield, weapon, two more, two drives; 0..4, GNPRTB 0x800), ship+0x60 hull damage, ship+0x50 bit 9 damaged (FUN_00501c00). FUN_00484630 (caller FUN_00433620, read in FUN_00433780) scales record attack and manoeuvre by the weapon loss and shield by the shield loss, keeps class hull, and sets 0x1000 (damaged, can jump) or 0x800000 (drives out, hyp). FUN_004749b0 and FUN_00477a40 split damaged ships off task fleets and regional records; module 11 phase 0x3f8 step 2 FUN_004c8e90 sends mobile damaged ships to the nearest own unblockaded shipyard-role system (sys+0x28 & 0x200000), else the nearest own unblockaded system. Repair: timer 0x380 every GNPRTB 0x805 = 30 days, or 0x804 = 2 days where the system holds a counted own shipyard (sys+0x88 bit 10); each step heals max hull / 10 and, at class damage control (cls+0xd8) percent, clears one counter point (FUN_00501c50 via FUN_0057c2c0). Port today: ship_record keeps class figures and never sets 0x1000/0x800000; phase 0x3f8 is empty; repair.rs repairs at any manufacturing facility, adds damage control to hull each tick, ignores counters; world/mod.rs names the counters shield/weapon_recharge_allocated. Steps: (1) counters on the ship and the rename, (2) ship_record scaling and flags, (3) FUN_004c8e90 in module 11, (4) repair.rs cadence. Save bump and golden for a named cause; telemetry_coverage repair.
notes: Landed (uncommitted): damage counters on ShipInstance (damage_counters nibbles, repair_timer, is_damaged; GNPRTB 0x800 divisor), combat write-back and tactical import of the counters (tactical/apply.rs, tactical.rs), ship_record scaling and 0x1000/0x800000 flags with fleet 0x1000/0x2000 and ready/laser-count exclusion (ai_records.rs), FUN_004c8e90 as module 11 phase 0x3f8 via Order::MoveShips -> CreateFleet (ai_production.rs, ai.rs), repair.rs on timer 0x380 (30/2 day cadence, max hull/10, damage-control roll per counter point from the sim roll stream), SAVE_VERSION 49. hyp: counters 8-11/12-15 = tractor/engines; timer spread 0; phase 0x3f8 steps 3-4 empty; no Move to own system. Replay golden not regenerated (initial fp v1:7e5c233c69c86cba).
close_reason: Ported and checked natively on both sides: Damage ship plus native repair telemetry show a ship at its own working yard repairing every 2 days (Alliance Fleet 3 at Mon Calamari, Empire Fleet 1 at Coruscant) and every 30 days without one or at an enemy system under blockade (Empire Fleet 1 at Corsin). An own blockaded yard never holds its holder's damaged ship (FUN_00515480); the rebelling-yard case is or-chore-uprising-at-command-6q65.

title: A loaded save reuses freed slotmap slots in a different order than the uninterrupted game
description:
Playtest staging (2026-10-16): a save at day 60 loaded and run 15 days diverges from the straight run (fingerprints cd7111ed2f3840a8 vs 654f1a00678d424a; equal at +10). A world JSON diff shows exactly one difference: a new manufacturing facility at manufacturing_facilities[47] version 3 (freed slot reused) in the straight run, [99] version 2 (fresh slot) after load. Every other world field matches, and the restored sim_rng and the other states are identical. So the slotmap free list is not restored in its pre-save order, and since the AI walks the world's slotmap order (e.g. ai_production scrap_system_fighter after the 2026-10-16 determinism fix) a loaded game plays differently. Fix: persist and restore each slotmap's free order (save bump), or allocate new objects in an order independent of slot reuse. Gate: agent_docs/simulation.md --load paragraph; hyp: the replay golden's save-reload test passes because its window frees no slot before the save (unverified).

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Stage a playtest game and save it at day 60.
2. Run the uninterrupted game 15 more days and record its fingerprint.
3. Load the day-60 save, run 15 days, and record its fingerprint.
4. The fingerprints differ (cd7111ed2f3840a8 vs 654f1a00678d424a): one new manufacturing facility takes a reused slot in the straight run and a fresh slot after the load.
acceptance_criteria:
- [x] A game loaded at day 60 and run 15 days matches the uninterrupted run's fingerprint.
- [x] A test reproduces the slot-order difference and fails before the fix.
notes:
Fixed: world slotmaps are saved as {slots, free} (crates/rebellion-core/src/world/slot_order.rs, serde(with) on the 11 GameWorld arenas, save v48). slotmap's serde keeps slots+versions but rebuilds the free list in descending index order; the adapter writes the pop order (probed on a clone) and rebuilds each map by remove/insert cycles to saved versions, freeing vacant slots in reverse pop order; rejects a free list that is not a permutation of the vacant slots. Proof (same binary): seed 42 and 7 save@60 +15 == straight 75; seed 42 save@300 +700 == straight 1000; seed 7 save@300 +300 == straight 600. Seed 7 straight runs are themselves nondeterministic between day 600 and 700 (same binary, three different fingerprints), unrelated to load. Replay golden: initial fingerprint no longer matches (free order is now in the canonical fingerprint); not regenerated.
2026-10-22: box ticked on review of the close reason, which names the evidence; the bead closed 2026-10-21, before the close policy. Seed 42 and 7 save@60 +15 match the straight runs (notes above).
2026-10-22: crates/rebellion-core/src/world/slot_order.rs test a_loaded_map_reuses_freed_slots_in_the_order_the_removals_left removes slots 1, 3 and 0, round-trips the map through serde and compares four inserts against the live map; on the Mini it fails with the reorder bypassed (load keeps slotmap's own free order) and passes with it.

title: Match Direct3D RM's 8-bit palette, line stepping and rasterizer for the tactical aperture
description:
Match Direct3D Retained Mode's 8-bit output so the tactical aperture's SSIM and edge IoU can pass, starting with TAC-05-C019.

The original draws the tactical scene through d3drm.dll, a system library outside the executable's trace, into an 8-bit paletted surface. A0 TAC-05-C019 (empire-death-star-pre-alert, day 676) holds 69 colours in the whole frame and 21 to 24 in the aperture (TAC-05-C017 21, TAC-05-C019 24).

What the port must match:
- Colour matching: every 3D pixel maps into the display palette. The scene background's greys (resource 5030, palette 5553) read 24, 40 and 58 in the port; A0 shows 0, 48 and 48.
- The scene background stretch: SetSceneBackgroundImage (frame slot 0xcc) draws the 440 by 438 image into the 439 by 437 viewport at (17, 30). Stars land one to two pixels from an unscaled copy, some as 2 by 2 blocks.
- The wireframe line stepping for the holocube (quality 0x40).
- Flat-shaded mesh rasterization and the scene's lights for the capital meshes.

Measured on C019 with the traced camera, 3D window and holocube (or-p-tactical-camera-viewport-aw39): 7,466 aperture edge pixels in A0 or A1, of which 5,350 coincide (edge IoU 0.717). The misses split as holocube 361, ships, fighters and strike 1,016, stars 739. Passing edge IoU 0.98 allows about 150.

C019 passes the C6 position measures (displacement, MAE, changed pixels) under a split recorded in tactical-a0-compare.json; its SSIM and edge IoU rows wait on this node.

Source: ghidra/notes/tactical-camera-holocube.md, "Open: the 8-bit frame".
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Palette matching, the background stretch, holocube line stepping and flat shading follow d3drm's 8-bit output, each tied to A0 measurements
- [ ] TAC-05-C019 passes SSIM and edge IoU in C6 with negative controls (Empire), and an Alliance aperture cell passes the same rows
notes:
With the capital meshes at their traced 3.0 scale (FUN_005d5b10) and the 0.3-unit fighter decals ported, C019 (empire-death-star-pre-alert, day 676) measures SSIM 0.952 and edge IoU 0.7185: 7,549 edge pixels in A0 or A1, 5,424 coinciding; misses holocube 412, ships, fighters and strike 977, stars 736. Its position measures pass: displacement 0, MAE 0.0023, changed pixels 0.0046 (903 of 194,916: holocube 221, ships 395, stars 287).
The tactical projection scale, (w+h)/4 per field unit with the half-pixel centre, is fitted to the A0 frames with a hyp: tag; the viewport projection lives in d3drm.dll, so tracing it belongs here.

title: Question: what sets and hides the task-force slot caption
description:
## Question

Where does a task-force slot's drawn caption come from, in which font is it selected, and why does an unassigned slot draw none?

What is known: the strobe button paints its `+200` string with `DrawTextA(.., DT_CENTER)` in rectangle `+0xcc` (`FUN_00602d30.c:80-90`). It does so only while `+200` holds a string and bit `0x20` of `+0xc4` is set (`:80-82`); the ctor sets `+0xc4 = 0x10020` and `+200 = 0` (`FUN_00602150.c:37`, `:74`). The rectangle is laid out by `FUN_006026e0.c:28-48`, in application font 4 (`FUN_005ff910.c:145-147`). `FUN_00413000.c:141` sets `+0xb0 = 4`; that this object is the `DAT_006be3b8` that `FUN_00603850` reads is inferred. `FUN_0060eed0` gives entry 4 lfHeight 16 (`:49-51`) and weight 400 (`:89`). Its face comes from `this+0x38` (`:26-47`), which `FUN_0060ee20` fills with "Arial" when `FUN_005ff830` builds the font table at `DAT_006be4f8` (`FUN_005ff830.c:5`, `FUN_0060ee20.c:13`, `:32`; `ghidra/notes/text-sources.md:90`). `ghidra/notes/galaxy-view-framing.md:221-245` tabulates all 14 entries: entry 4 is Arial, lfHeight 16, weight 400, lfQuality 2. What stays open is that the caption selects entry 4 (`FUN_006002c0`, and the `DAT_006be3b8` inference above).

`FUN_0059be80.c:66-69` calls `FUN_005ef240(this, slot, &{0xad81+i, DAT_0065d428}, &{0xad92, DAT_0065d428})`. Argument 2 is likely the caption (TEXTTACT `0xad81+i`) and argument 3 the hover text. The controls that draw no number pass 0 as argument 2: the task-force header with `0xad91` (`FUN_0059be80.c:43-44`), the fighter header with `0xad9b` (`FUN_0059c030.c:40-41`) and the fighter slots with `0xad9d+i` (`FUN_0059c030.c:61-62`). `FUN_005ef240` is not on disk. A0 `TAC-02-C006` shows no glyph on unassigned slot 3. `FUN_00600c40` sets hover text, not the caption (`FUN_00600cc0.c:13-21`).

## Where to look

- `FUN_005ef240`. The panel base's vtable `+0x4c`, which `FUN_005e1550.c:29`, `:37` call as `(button, 0, &key)`, has the shape of `FUN_005ef240(this, button, caption, hover)` here (`FUN_0059be80.c:44`, `:69`); `or-q-panel-button-caption-v6t` asks what that slot does with the key. If one resolves to the other, one note answers both and the other bead cites it.
- `FUN_005c5480` and `FUN_005c54d0`: does either clear `+200` or bit `0x20`? The input question (`or-ep-task-force-strip-5kdd.2`) asks which `+0xc4` bits they set; one reading of the two decompiles answers both beads, and the second note cites the first.
- The paint override in vtable `0x0066ca60`.
- `FUN_006002c0` (font select), `FUN_005f2fc0`, `DAT_0065d428`.
- TEXTTACT RT_STRING `0xad81`-`0xad88`, `0xad91`, `0xad92`, `0xad9b`, `0xad9d`-`0xada0`.
- The eight task-slot records `+0xd8`..`+0xf4`, stored by `FUN_0059a8d0.c:37-44` and passed by `FUN_0059b450.c:25,40`.
- The Feature Wiki map pages `executable/map-18-5c2990` (`FUN_005c5480`, `FUN_005c54d0`), `executable/map-20-5e9bcb` (`FUN_005ef240`) and `executable/map-21-5fd7c0` (`FUN_006002c0`, the CoolStrobeButton) give each function's role and proposed name.

Check both sides wherever the code branches.
acceptance_criteria:
- [x] A note in ghidra/notes/ names the caption's source string and setter with function and line citations
- [x] The note states which application font entry the caption selects (FUN_006002c0, and whether the +0xb0 = 4 of FUN_00413000.c:141 is on the DAT_006be3b8 that FUN_00603850 reads), and cites ghidra/notes/galaxy-view-framing.md:221-245 and ghidra/notes/text-sources.md:90 for that entry's face, height and weight
- [x] The note explains why an unassigned slot draws no caption (A0 TAC-02-C006 slot 3), citing FUN_005c5480/FUN_005c54d0 or the paint override
- [x] The TEXTTACT ids used by both strips are listed with their roles (caption or hover)
- [x] Every cited decompile is attached in ghidra/notes/

title: Unassigned task-force slots act only in the original's modes
description:
## Background

An unassigned task-force slot ignores a click unless `FUN_00595b90` -> `FUN_0059a520` -> `FUN_0059f6e0` holds: mode `0xe` with the controller flag, or mode `0x10` (`FUN_0059b450.c:18-19`, `FUN_0059f6e0.c:7-13`). When it holds, the slot takes its hover text (`FUN_00600c40`, which sets hover text, not the caption: `FUN_00600cc0.c:13-21`) and its images (`FUN_005c5480`), presses (state 5, `FUN_006030c0`) and posts command 2+i (`FUN_0059b450.c:39-44`). The executor passes that command to the current mode's `+0x14(i)` only while the controller flag `*this` is set (`FUN_0059fd40.c:33-38`). In mode `0x10` with the flag clear, the command calls no `+0x14`.

Whether an unassigned slot can be clicked at all, or is reached only by keys 1-8, is the input question's to settle (`or-ep-task-force-strip-5kdd.2`). The modes and their `+0x14` are the modes question's (`.3`). The port assigns with Ctrl+click and a next-blank rule (`crates/rebellion-render/src/tactical_view.rs:3116-3141`, `:4944-4961`), tested at `:9601-9618` against manual pp. 143 and 148; no traced function checks it (inferred). The A1 yaga `task-force-2` journey (`TAC-03-C014`/`C015`) depends on today's input, and `tools/interface-parity/run.mjs:1784-1797` asserts an unassigned slot press logs no `[tactical_groups]` line.

## Scope

Replace or reconcile the Ctrl+click path with the modes the modes question names, entered through the input path the input question names. Change the `:9601` test only with the question's evidence, cited. Keep the yaga `task-force-2` journey reproducing its cells, and change its input only with the traced path, named in the commit.

## Tests

## E2E

## Evidence

## Constraints

AGENTS.md applies: both factions, cited original behaviour, red-first tests in a Mini clone, Mini-only cargo, silent runs, the browser only through the interface-parity gates, no commit before Tom's word.

title: Native check of both group strips on both sides
description:
## Background

The strip ports change clicks, keys, labels and pressed looks. The tactical HUD has no named controls, so the native check uses raw coordinates (`agent_docs/dev-commands.md`). Task-force slot n (1-8) is centred at x = 43 + 29n, y 10 (`FUN_0059be80.c:55`: x `0x3c + 0x1d*i`, y 2, 25x17); fighter slot n (1-4) at x = 330 + 29n, y 9 (`FUN_0059c030.c:52`: x `0x15b + 0x1d*i`, y 2, 25x15).

## E2E

On the Mini, silent: `scripts/launch-native.sh --live --seed <n>`, then a `scripts/dev-run.sh` batch, once with `Start game: Empire` and once with `Start game: Alliance`. Record the seed. The briefing and the Advice index hold the clock until skipped and closed, and the policies do not act during `Wait until battle alert` (`agent_docs/dev-commands.md`; the same opening as `scripts/native-checks/scheduler-battle-hold-empire.txt`):

`Press` releases at once, so a held key's look is not checked here. Entering the assignment modes is `or-ep-task-force-strip-5kdd.10`'s native check.

title: Question: do the strip bitmaps' FUN_005fd170 keys equal the first stored pixel the port keys on?
description:
## Question

Do the strip bitmaps' transparent keys, as the original sets them, equal the first stored pixel the port keys on?

What is known: `FUN_005fd0f0` passes a loaded bitmap's `+8` and `+9` as the transparent key for 8-bit and colour blits (`FUN_005fd0f0.c:13-16`), and the strobe button blits its images through it (`FUN_00602d30.c:68`). The loader `FUN_005fbd20` calls `FUN_005fc500` and then, when bits are loaded (`+4`), `FUN_005fd170` (`FUN_005fbd20.c:15-18`). For an 8-bit bitmap `FUN_005fd170` stores in `+8` the first stored byte when the header's compression (`+0x10`) is not 1; for RLE8 (1) it stores the first run's colour byte, or the first byte of a leading absolute run (escape above 2), else 0 (`FUN_005fd170.c:10-24`). For a 24-bit bitmap it stores the first pixel's three bytes, reversed, at `+9`-`+0xb` (`:29-33`). `ghidra/notes/tactical-results.md:78-81` reads the result, index 252, palette blue, on the results marks and tabs. Every strip state image loads through `FUN_005fbd20`: the ctors (`FUN_00602150.c:48`, `:63`; `FUN_005c52e0.c:27`, `:37`) and the state setter `FUN_00603150` (`:24`), which `FUN_0059be80.c:62-63` uses. The port keys a strobe-button bitmap on its first stored pixel (`BmpCache::get_macroquad_button`, `crates/rebellion-render/src/bmp_cache.rs:1744`; the hit mask at `:1507-1509` reads uncompressed rows). `ghidra/notes/gid-legend.md:83` notes a palette-blue first pixel on the GID legend bitmaps.

What stays open is the data: each strip bitmap's compression and first stored byte, which show where a leading RLE8 escape (key 0) or run would make the port's key differ.

## Where to look

The strip bitmaps by resource id (`ghidra/notes/tactical-group-strips.md:20-25`): headers 1001, 1004, 1008 and 1010; task-force slots 1005, 1006 and 1007; fighter slots 1012-1015, 1016-1019 and 1020. `FUN_005fc500`, `FUN_005fc040`, `FUN_005fc100`, `FUN_005fc710` and `FUN_0060e710` only if a bitmap's header is unusual.
acceptance_criteria:
- [x] A note in ghidra/notes/ states what +8 (8-bit) and +9 to +0xb (24-bit) of a loaded bitmap hold, citing FUN_005fd170.c:10-33 and FUN_005fbd20.c:15-18, with the RLE8 cases
- [x] The note gives, by resource id, each strip bitmap's compression, first stored byte and resulting key (headers 1001, 1004, 1008, 1010; slots 1005-1007 and 1012-1020, fighter slot 1012 included), and says where the port's first-stored-pixel key (bmp_cache.rs:1744) differs
- [x] Every cited decompile is attached in ghidra/notes/
notes: ghidra/notes/strip-bitmap-keys.md: all sixteen strip bitmaps are uncompressed 8-bit, so the original's +8 key is the first stored byte, the byte the port keys on; no bitmap differs. Keys: headers 1001/1008 24, 1004 15, 1010 23; slots 1005, 1012-1015, 1020 key 17; 1006, 1016-1019 key 15; 1007 keys 10.
close_reason: Keys equal the port's for every strip bitmap

title: Question: strobe-button proc, disabled slots and key presses
description:
## Question

Is `FUN_006028c0` the strip buttons' proc? What does the fighter builder's vtable `+0x10` call do to a slot? Is an unassigned task-force slot disabled, so that a click never reaches `FUN_0059b450`? What does the parent do with the message the proc posts on press? Does a number key's programmatic press post the slot's command and end itself?

What is known: `FUN_006028c0` calls `FUN_006035f0` on `WM_LBUTTONDOWN` (`:89-105`) and again on release before posting `WM_COMMAND` (`:163-194`). On press it also posts message `0x40e` to the parent with the control id (`:104-105`). `FUN_006035f0.c:10-38` reads flags `+0xc4`: bit 2, or no image for the state, gives no hit (`:24-26`), bit `0x10` a bitmap hit (`FUN_005fca00`), otherwise x <= `+0x38` and y <= `+0x3c`, which `FUN_005ff910.c:135-136` stores as width and height. The ctor ORs bit `0x10` only when its last argument is 0 (`FUN_00602150.c:115-116`). Both slot builders pass 1 (`FUN_005c52e0.c:17-18`, `FUN_0059c030.c:52-53`) and both headers 0 (`FUN_0059be80.c:39`, `FUN_0059c030.c:35`), so slots hit their rectangle and headers their bitmap. That `FUN_006028c0` is the proc of vtable `0x0066df58` is inferred from shared fields (`+0xc4`, `+0xf8`).

`FUN_0059c030.c:63` makes an argument-less vtable `+0x10` call on each fighter slot. Bit 2 forces paint state 2 (`FUN_00602d30.c:12-15`) and blocks the hit (`FUN_006035f0.c:24-26`), so if `+0x10` sets bit 2, a disabled slot takes no click.

Unassigned task-force slots: `FUN_0059be80.c:62` gives every slot's state-2 image the unassigned bitmap 1007, and `:65` calls `FUN_005c54d0` on every slot. State 2 paints `+0x9c` in colour `+0xc0` (`FUN_00602d30.c:26-33`). If `FUN_005c54d0` sets bit 2, an unassigned slot takes no click, and `FUN_0059b450`'s unassigned branch (`:39-44`) is reached only by the key path. If it does not, a click outside the assignment modes flips the slot's pressed bit 4 on release (toggle bit 8, `FUN_006028c0.c:186-188`) while `FUN_0059b450` returns without releasing it (`:18-19`, `:53`). A0 `TAC-02-C012`, a click on blank slot 3, has the same frame hash as the rest frame `TAC-02-C008` (`docs/qa/2026-09-10-interface-parity-audit/evidence/2026-10-13-tactical-a0-capture-index.md`), so that click changed nothing visible.

Keys 1-8 press a slot through `FUN_0059ca90(.., 1)` -> `FUN_00603710` (`FUN_0059b730.c:58-97`); no key-up case exists for them (`:133-179`). The proc clears bit 1 and releases capture on a `WM_COMMAND` carrying its own id (`FUN_006028c0.c:133-148`), which fits `FUN_00603710` ending its own press.

The map gives the CoolStrobeButton's state images at `+0x94` normal, `+0x98` pressed, `+0x9c` disabled and `+0xa0` selected, and its click sound at `+0xdc` with the sound object at `+0xe0` (`ghidra/notes/rebexe-map.md:690-694`, from Feature Wiki `executable/map-21-5fd7c0`). `FUN_00602840` stores a control's sound id at `+0xdc` (`ghidra/notes/audio-dispatch.md:24`); it has 53 call sites in 15 windows, and `FUN_00603710` and `FUN_006028c0` play it (`:59`). None of `FUN_0059be80.c`, `FUN_0059c030.c` and `FUN_005c52e0.c` calls `FUN_00602840`, so the press-sound question comes down to `FUN_005ef240` and the call-site list (Feature Wiki `executable/mod-audio`, `audio-dispatch.md:12`), which `or-q-control-sound-modules-eybm` also walks. A fighter slot whose group is cleared (`FUN_005a0320`) draws state 2 and takes no click (`ghidra/notes/tactical-group-strips.md:39-45`); A0 `TAC-05-C023` shows the Red slot greyed after order 6 (`ghidra/notes/tactical-command-assignment.md:93-103`).

## Where to look

Vtable `0x0066df58` (its `+0x10`, `+0x14` and the window proc it registers), `FUN_005c54d0`, `FUN_005c5480`, the tactical window's handler for `0x40e` (vtable `0x0066bb00`, ctor `FUN_0059a8d0`), `FUN_00603710`, `FUN_00603780`, `FUN_00602510`, `FUN_00603120`, `FUN_006030c0`, `FUN_006030f0`. The caption question (`.1`) also reads `FUN_005c54d0`/`FUN_005c5480`, so the two notes may share those decompiles.
acceptance_criteria:
- [x] A note confirms or refutes that FUN_006028c0 is the CoolStrobeButton proc, with citations
- [x] The note states what vtable +0x10 sets on a fighter slot and what a click on such a slot does
- [x] The note states what FUN_005c54d0 and FUN_005c5480 set on a task-force slot, whether an unassigned slot is disabled (+0xc4 bit 2), and what a click on an unassigned slot does outside modes 0xe and 0x10, squared with A0 TAC-02-C012
- [x] The note states what the tactical window does with message 0x40e, which the proc posts on press (FUN_006028c0.c:104-105)
- [x] The note settles whether FUN_00603710 posts the slot's command (and so whether keys 1-8 reach FUN_0059b450's unassigned branch) and how the pressed state is released
- [x] The note states whether any strip slot or header gets a press sound: whether FUN_005ef240, either strip builder or another FUN_00602840 call site sets +0xdc on them, which the proc plays on press (FUN_006028c0.c:106-108; ghidra/notes/audio-dispatch.md:24, :59), both sides
- [x] Every cited decompile is attached in ghidra/notes/
notes: ghidra/notes/tactical-strip-buttons.md: FUN_006028c0 is the proc (FUN_00600310 forwards to vtable +0x14). Fighter +0x10 = FUN_006028a0 disables (bit 2, EnableWindow FALSE): no click. An unassigned task-force slot is enabled and takes a click, which changes nothing outside modes 0xe/0x10 (1007/1007, no toggle bit; A0 TAC-02-C012 = C008). 0x40e is ignored. FUN_00603710 posts WM_COMMAND(id) to the parent, so keys reach FUN_0059b450 including the unassigned branch; the key's held bit stays until the next key, another slot click or a release on that slot. Hit test inclusive (x <= 25, y <= 17). No strip control has a press sound. No side branch beyond the header bitmaps.

title: Question: tactical selection modes 0xe, 0x10, 0x11 and the unassigned-slot handler
description:
## Question

What are the tactical UI modes with ids `0xe`, `0x10` and `0x11`, what does an unassigned task-force slot do in them, and does an F-key follow camera change the selection?

What is known: `FUN_0059b450.c:18-19` lets an unassigned slot act only when `FUN_0059f6e0` holds: mode id `0xe` with the controller's `*this` set, or `0x10` (`FUN_0059f6e0.c:7-13`). The executor `FUN_0059fd40.c:24-88` installs task-force mode `FUN_005a33d0(i)` or fighter mode `FUN_005a4640(i)`, returns to the base mode `FUN_005a0c80` when the same slot is clicked again (ids 1-8 and 9-12 by comparison), and calls the current mode's `+0x14(i)` for an unassigned slot when `*this != 0`; the fighter case has no such fallback and breaks with no mode (`:67-68`). The controller flag `*this` is toggled by command `0x7b` (`FUN_0059fd40.c:168-193`, via `FUN_005c7e10`) and cleared by `0x7a` (`:157`). `FUN_0059e760.c:11-31` acts per group only for mode ids 1-12, through callees not on disk. F1-F12 call `FUN_005c2990(camera, 0xb, i)`, a follow camera `FUN_005d9a70` (`FUN_005c2990.c:87-114`). The port assigns with Ctrl+click and a next-blank rule, tested at `crates/rebellion-render/src/tactical_view.rs:9601-9618` against manual pp. 143 and 148; no traced function checks it (inferred from the files read). Entering the base mode runs `FUN_005c0e70`, `FUN_005c0e60` and `FUN_005c0e80` (`FUN_005a0c80.c:16-18`); `FUN_005c0e80` shows panel `0x15`, nothing selected (`ghidra/notes/tactical-command-assignment.md:83-84`, `:96`), so what remains is what `FUN_005c0e60` and `FUN_005c0e70` clear. Camera mode `0xb` takes `FUN_005c2990`'s default case, which builds `FUN_005d9a70` (vtable `0x0066d478`, `FUN_005d9a70.c:14-20`) and keeps or builds the `FUN_005d9580` camera (`FUN_005c2990.c:87-114`). `or-q-tac-camera-e1d` asks where modes 7-11 place the camera; this bead asks only whether the follow camera changes the selection, and each note links the other.

## Where to look

The `+8` id of every mode class: `FUN_005a0c80` (vtable `0x0066be30`), `FUN_005a33d0` (`0x0066bc48`), `FUN_005a4640`, and the classes returning `0xe`, `0x10`, `0x11`; their `+0x14`; commands `0x7a`/`0x7b` and `FUN_005c7e10`; `FUN_0059f5d0`, `FUN_0059f5f0`, `FUN_0059fc50`, `FUN_005c1040`, `FUN_005c0e40`, `FUN_005c0e60`/`70`/`80` (the `FUN_0059e760` callees); `FUN_005d9a70`; callers of `FUN_005a0410`; the input path for Ctrl+click on a ship. Both sides. The Feature Wiki map pages `executable/map-16-58ef80` (`FUN_0059e760`, `FUN_0059f5d0`-`FUN_0059fd40`, `FUN_005a0410`, `FUN_005a0c80`, `FUN_005a33d0`, `FUN_005a4640`), `executable/map-17-5a54ee` (`FUN_005c0e40`-`FUN_005c1040`), `executable/map-18-5c2990` (`FUN_005c2990`, `FUN_005c7e10`) and `executable/map-19-5d895e` (`FUN_005d9a70`) give each function's role.

- [x] The note names modes 0xe, 0x10 and 0x11, the controller flag commands 0x7a/0x7b toggle, and what an unassigned slot click does in each mode (their +0x14, and the executor's *this gate, FUN_0059fd40.c:34-37)
- [x] The note states which slot FUN_0059e760 presses in modes 1-12, from its callees
- [x] The note states what FUN_005c0e60 and FUN_005c0e70 do when the base mode FUN_005a0c80 is entered (FUN_005a0c80.c:16-18): whether the ship and fighter selections clear; the panel it shows is 0x15 (FUN_005c0e80; ghidra/notes/tactical-command-assignment.md:83-84, :96)
- [x] The note states which mode a ship pick in the 3D view installs and whether it presses or releases a strip slot, squared with A0 TAC-03-C018

title: Decision: how C6 judges the task-force labels' glyphs
description:
## Background

A0 draws the slot numbers as aliased GDI Arial, black or white, with no intermediate greys (`TAC-02-C006`, `TAC-02-C011`). The port draws anti-aliased text. Tom accepted anti-aliased port text on 2026-10-14 where content, size and position match, but the C6 changed-pixel gate (0.5 %, delta > 2) fails anti-aliased glyphs, and `agent_docs/task-graph.md` ("The chain") allows a mask only with proof of nondeterminism and a written justification; anti-aliasing is not nondeterminism. The browser gate already masks the labels (`labelMask` `{4,2,17,14}`, `tools/interface-parity/run.mjs:4474`, used at `:4511`, `:4535-4542`, `:4676`), which the same rule covers.

## Design

Options: (a) draw these labels aliased (alpha thresholded at 0.5), so the region can match exactly and `labelMask` can go; (b) keep anti-aliased glyphs under a documented threshold decision by Tom, outside the mask rule, recorded in the plan and the compare spec, that compares the label rows by glyph position and size instead of pixels. A plain mask is rejected.

`or-dec-c6-text-masks-rue` asks Tom the same question for every text region C6 compares (`TAC-03-C019`'s status panel fails at SSIM 0.952, 3.7 % changed): measured label masks, each citing that decision, plus a separate check that the strings, positions and em size match A0. That is option (b) applied to every text region. Decide the two together: if Tom approves it, (b) here cites that decision; if he chooses (a) for these labels, the record says why they differ from the other text regions.

## Constraints

AGENTS.md applies: both factions, cited original behaviour, red-first tests in a Mini clone, Mini-only cargo, silent runs, the browser only through the interface-parity gates, no commit before Tom's word.
acceptance_criteria:
- [x] Tom has chosen (a) aliased labels or (b) a documented threshold decision for the label rows
- [x] The choice says what happens to run.mjs's labelMask
- [x] The choice and its reason are recorded in the plan doc
- [x] The choice cites Tom's decision on or-dec-c6-text-masks-rue, or says why the task-force labels differ from it
notes:
Tom chose (a) on 2026-10-21: the task-force numbers are drawn aliased (coverage thresholded at 0.5), so task-force-strip and task-force-1 match pixel for pixel and run.mjs's labelMask {4,2,17,14} is removed. They differ from or-dec-c6-text-masks-rue because each is one or two glyphs filling a 25x17 slot, where a mask would hide the whole label; the longer text regions take rue's masks, which Tom approved the same day. Recorded in docs/plans/2026-10-20-feat-task-force-strip.md, Decisions.
Tom, 2026-10-21, on seeing that GDI Arial's digits (a footless 1, other curves on 2 and 3) cannot come from Liberation Sans: keep the port's smoothed Liberation Sans for the slot numbers, at font 4's size and the original's centred place. C6 masks each caption cell under or-dec-c6-text-masks-rue (task-force-caption-1..8 in tactical-a0-compare.json); the label unit tests check the digit, place and size.
close_reason: Tom chose aliased labels (a); recorded in the plan doc

title: Draw the task-force slot labels in font 4 with the state colours
description:
## Background

The strobe button paints its caption centred in the slot (`FUN_00602d30.c:80-90`, layout `FUN_006026e0.c:28-48`: left = (25 - w)/2, top = (17 - h)/2 in integers) in application font 4, a 16-pixel cell (`FUN_005ff910.c:145-147`, `FUN_0060eed0.c:49-51`; the face, Arial, is the caption question's to confirm). Text is black normally (`FUN_00602150.c:75`), white when pressed (`FUN_0059be80.c:64`, painted at `FUN_00602d30.c:57`), and white while held (`+0xb8`, `FUN_00602150.c:76`, painted at `FUN_00602d30.c:20-23`). Both sides share the code; only the header bitmap branches (`FUN_0059be80.c:27-32`). The port draws 13 px, baseline 16, always black (`crates/rebellion-render/src/tactical_view.rs:4064-4085`).

A0 frames of the labels:

title: Strip slots take a click anywhere in their rectangle
description:
## Background

The strip slots hit-test their client rectangle. `FUN_006035f0.c:24-38` uses a bitmap hit only when flag `0x10` of `+0xc4` is set, and the CoolStrobeButton ctor ORs that bit only when its last argument is 0 (`FUN_00602150.c:115-116`). Both slot builders pass 1 (`FUN_005c52e0.c:17-18`, `FUN_0059c030.c:52-53`). Both headers pass 0 (`FUN_0059be80.c:39`, `FUN_0059c030.c:35`) and keep a bitmap hit. A disabled button (bit 2), or one with no image for its state, takes no hit (`FUN_006035f0.c:24-26`). `FUN_006028c0` runs the test on press (`:89-105`) and on release before posting the command (`:163-194`). `+0x38`/`+0x3c` are the control's width and height (`FUN_005ff910.c:135-136`). A press lands only inside the window. A release counts at local x <= width and y <= height (`FUN_006035f0.c:33-34`): x <= 25 and y <= 17 on a task-force slot, x <= 25 and y <= 15 on a fighter slot (`FUN_0059be80.c:55`, `FUN_0059c030.c:52`).

The held look is fixed at button-down. The proc passes bit 1 of `+0xc4` as the paint state (`FUN_006028c0.c:27-28`). Paint state 1 draws the held image and colour only while `+0xf8` is set (`FUN_00602d30.c:19-25`), and `+0xf8` is set only by the hit test (`FUN_006035f0.c:30,35`). The proc has no `WM_MOUSEMOVE` (0x200) case; that message falls to `DefWindowProcA` (`FUN_006028c0.c:53-55`, `:89-133`). So dragging off a held slot keeps it held. The port recomputes the held look from the pointer each frame (`pressed_tactical_hud_control`, `tactical_view.rs:3381-3391`).

The port instead requires an opaque bitmap pixel for both strips (`tactical_hud_control_at`, `crates/rebellion-render/src/tactical_view.rs:2603-2636`). title: Group-selection mode with toggling slot clicks on both strips
description:
## Background

An assigned task-force slot posts command 2+i and releases every other assigned slot (`FUN_0059b450.c:27-37`); an existing fighter slot posts `0xb+i` and releases the others (`FUN_0059b620.c:12-30`); a missing group does nothing. The executor installs task-force mode `FUN_005a33d0(i)` or fighter mode `FUN_005a4640(i)`, and a second click on the selected slot returns to the base mode `FUN_005a0c80`, clearing the selection (`FUN_0059fd40.c:24-88`); the fighter case has no fallback for a missing group (`:67-68`). The button toggles itself: every slot carries toggle bit 8 (`FUN_0059be80.c:61`, `FUN_0059c030.c:58`), and on release a hit flips its pressed bit 4 before `WM_COMMAND` is posted (`FUN_006028c0.c:184-192`), while `FUN_0059b450`/`FUN_0059b620` release only the others (`FUN_006030f0(5)` clears bits 1 and 4). `FUN_0059e760.c:11-31` acts per group only in modes 1-12 (its callees are the modes question's); A0 `TAC-03-C018` shows slot 1 unpressed after a ship click. The port always reselects (`select_task_force`, `crates/rebellion-render/src/tactical_view.rs:3092`; `select_fighter_group`, `:3162`) and presses the slot of whatever ships are selected (`selected_player_task_force`, `:2992`).

## Scope

`crates/rebellion-core/src/tactical.rs`: a non-serialized group-selection mode on `BattleSession` (task force i or fighter group i). `tactical_view.rs`: a second click clears ships and the mode; a ship pick in the 3D view clears the mode; the pressed look reads the mode, which must equal the button's own toggle. Say what a deselect does to `command_panel` (today a click sets `Display`, `:4954`). Keep `selected_player_task_force` for focus targets, navigation and the voice cue (`:3016-3140`, `:3354`, tests `:9622-9760`); `task_force_and_fighter_group_selection_are_mutually_exclusive` (`:9560`) stays green. Keep the `[tactical_groups]` strings `run.mjs:4683-4688` matches (`task_force_selected slot=.. members=..`, `fighter_group_selected slot=.. members=..`, logged at `:4956`, `:4974`), and add `task_force_cleared slot=..` and `fighter_group_cleared slot=..` for a deselect.

## Tests

title: Number keys 1-8 and F1-F12 on the group strips

## Background

Save `empire-sixteen-tie-day415.sav` (`tools/original-capture/saves/INDEX.md`, row empire-sixteen-tie) is a new Empire game, Huge galaxy, Easy, saved at Coruscant on day 415. Fleet 1 holds all eight Imperial capitals and 16 TIE squadrons. Dragging Fleet 1 to Xyquine (Corellian sector, Alliance) opens the Battle at Xyquine alert about 21 days later.

The A0 cells (`docs/qa/2026-09-10-interface-parity-audit/evidence/2026-10-13-tactical-a0-capture-index.md`, rows TAC-02-C001 to C007):

- `TAC-02-C003`, `C004`, `C005` and `C007` are one frame, paused at Take Command. Task forces 1-4 are assigned, and slots 5-8 are unassigned (bitmap 1007, `FUN_0059be80`). The 16 squadrons split into Red, Blue, Green and Gold (`FUN_005ae460`), all present. C003 to C005 compare `fighter-group-strip`, and C007 compares `task-force-strip`.
- `TAC-02-C001`: each of the four two-ship task forces is split by hand into the blank slots, giving task forces 1-8 with one capital each. Slot 8 is pressed, with a white "8". The cell compares `task-force-strip`.

Their A1 pairs today are `production-group-presentation/task-force-8-selected` (C001), `production-group-presentation/actual` (C003-C005) and `production-participants/task-force-unassigned-released` (C007) (`tools/interface-parity/scenarios/tactical-a0-compare.json:74-80`). ## Scope

An A1 scenario in `tools/interface-parity/scenarios/tactical.catalog.json` for the Battle at Xyquine, after the pattern of `coruscant-day1173` (`state_match`, journey). Add a `state_matches` entry for `empire-sixteen-tie`, and point C003-C005 and C007 at its Take Command frame and C001 at a split frame. The split takes the port's task-force assignment input. `or-ep-task-force-strip-5kdd.10` replaces that input with the original's modes, so name the input used here; `.10` keeps this journey reproducing C001. The battle gate on the new scenario, both viewports, then `node tools/interface-parity/tactical-a0-compare.mjs --a1-run <run> --negative-controls`. The save is Empire-only, and the Alliance strip cells come from `or-ep-task-force-strip-5kdd.12` and `TAC-05-C023`.

title: Fix: telemetry_coverage finds no manufacturing or blockade events in the 1000-tick dual-AI playtest
description: crates/rebellion-data/tests/telemetry_coverage.rs (ignored; needs data/base) fails at a76109b8: Required systems with zero telemetry events: manufacturing, blockade. Decide whether the systems stopped emitting GameEventRecords or the dual-AI run no longer builds or blockades in 1000 ticks, then fix the cause, not the expectation.
notes:
Cause (2026-10-15): the dual-AI run queues no production. evaluate_production (ai.rs) is a sourceless heuristic with fixed thresholds (5 capital ships, 3 fighters per ship, 2 regiments, 2 defences, 5 yards per system). Seed 42 standard galaxy, fresh state: the Empire holds 9 systems with its shipyards and queues 0 items, being above every threshold; the Alliance queues 2 capital ships, then saturates. A 120-day dual-AI playtest emits 72 DispatchMission, 16 DispatchResearch, 2 MoveFleet, 0 EnqueueProduction. Fix: port the original production modules 1, 2, 3, 5, 6, 7, 10, 11 (ai-order-emission.md); their budgets are being traced. The blockade count follows from fleets never being built.
Plan (2026-10-15): port production modules 1, 2, 3, 5, 6, 7, 10, 11 in a new ai_production.rs replacing evaluate_production (docs/plans/2026-10-15-feat-original-ai-and-research.md, Phase C).
Progress (2026-10-15): with the original production modules (ai_production.rs), manufacturing and blockade now emit; the test fails only on repair. Repair needs a damaged ship at a system with a manufacturing facility. In the test galaxy (default SeedOptions, the Alliance as the player side) the Alliance starts over its maintenance capacity (load 132 of 100: 2 mines, 10 refineries), so module 2 scraps a yard and module 11 scraps its capital ships as decompiled (FUN_004e2760, FUN_004caad0). The 600-day dual-AI run then has 3 space battles, and no damaged Empire fleet returns to a yard. Returning a damaged fleet is module 8's fleet work (Phase C2-C4, which replaces evaluate_fleet_deployment); recheck repair after it.
2026-10-15: with the original strategic AI (modules 8, 9, 12, 13 ported), telemetry_coverage misses combat, blockade and repair. A 1000-day dual-AI playtest (seed 42) issues no Move of a fleet: each side's regional record (module 8) stays short of ships because the Empire's only warships sit in the HQ fleet task (module 9, fleet flag 0x8, not 0x4, so FUN_004782a0 skips them), module 11 builds transports (FUN_004ca5e0 bit 4 or c+0x260 < c+0x20c), and the capital ship budget turns negative under the standing maintenance shortfall, so module 11 scraps them. The root is or-pfrm: ten systems go Uncontrolled on day 1 and no system joins a side, so both economies stay at 2-3 systems. The heuristic AI it replaced attacked regardless, which is why combat appeared before. Blocked on or-pfrm.
2026-10-15 after or-pfrm: still passive. Probe (removed) per AI round over 300 days: module 13 marks one sector with a kind per side (rarely two), so each side runs one regional record (create_or_delete needs sum(sector.sync) < 0). Empire record: posture kind 2, 0 ships until ~day 240, then 1. Alliance record: posture kind 3/4, 1-4 ships. Postures end each pass at state 0; 24 orders in 600 passes. 1000 days: 48 fleet arrivals, 1-2 space battles, 7297 Diplomacy dispatches. Next: how many sectors FUN_ module 13's controller plans in the original (ai_strategy plan writes, set_mark kind != 0), and whether the Empire's warships stay in the HQ fleet task (flag 0x8 without 0x4) by design.
Native (2026-10-15, seed 42, player Empire, .artifacts/native-checks/2026-10-15-pfrm-empire): the Alliance AI's fleets at Ghorman, Hoth and Yavin leave by day 12 and stand together at Vagran on day 40; the Empire's 6 fleets stay at Coruscant (the HQ fleet task). Plan growth (controller state 2, +0x14) needs every record to carry +0x60 bit 0x80000, which FUN_00479a00 sets only when need & 0x4ff == 0 or (need & 0x9fe00000 and need & 0x1f == 0); the Empire record's need stays 0x18b (ship shortfalls), so n stays 1. 27 destroyed_on_arrival in 1000 days are fighters ordered for a fleet merged away before delivery (delivery.rs, Destination::Fleet).
2026-10-15 Death Star class: the Empire HQ fleet task gathered every Empire warship because its threshold (c+0x164, the best attack class) was 18000, the Death Star's attack. ai_production.rs capital_ship (FUN_004739b0) tested class.dat_id.family() in 0x18..=0x1b, which is 0 for the bare CAPSHPSD record id, so the Death Star counted as a combat class. In CAPSHPSD only record 136 (the Death Star) carries per-record family 0x18 (file +0x10); the test is now class.is_death_star(). After: threshold 2000 (ISD), the HQ task keeps one ISD, the Uvena ship joins a regional record and moves Sullust -> Drall -> Hoth, the Empire builds at Bortras. Golden regenerated (cause named in agent_docs/deterministic-replay.md). 1000-day playtest (seed 42): control 8/8/84, 90 fleet arrivals, 7 space battles, 7 bombardments, 1 blockade (Xyquine, day 929), 0 repair. telemetry_coverage: every system emits except blockade and repair. Why: in all 7 battles the winner (the Empire) takes no hull damage (hull before = after), the loser loses every ship, so no damaged ship ever reaches a yard; the Empire's regional fleet (posture kind 2, which records visited systems) gets its next Move the day it arrives, and the port evaluates the blockade rule after the AI's orders in the tick (simulation.rs), so a sweeping fleet is gone before the rule sees it. When the original reruns FUN_0050b8e0 (system slot +0xc8) relative to fleet arrival and AI orders is untraced (blockade-bit.md). Open: trace the slot +0xc8 caller, and whether an unplayed battle's winner takes hull damage in the original.
Original (VM, 2026-10-15, alliance-day54-advice.sav played on unattended at Fast to day 429, every Battle Alert set to auto-resolve; captures in .artifacts/vm/empire-ai-2026-10-15): no Battle Alert opened; the Message Index holds three Popular Support messages (Umgul, Bpfassh, Bothawui join the Empire) and three Conflict messages (Saboteurs Strike at Praesitlyn twice, at Denab), nothing else. The original Empire AI makes no fleet attack on the Alliance and no blockade the Alliance sees in its first 429 days of a Standard game, so a 1000-day run without blockades is within the original's behaviour; the port's Empire attacks earlier (Hoth, day 271, seed 42).
Blockade timing (2026-10-15, Ghidra, ghidra/notes/blockade-bit.md 'When it runs'): the original reruns FUN_0050b8e0 only on event 0x311 (requested by system bit 0x100000, FUN_0050ac10, from FUN_00508660 slot +0xc8 on any fleet or squadron usable-bit change). An arriving fleet's timer 0x387 and the events it raises, down to 0x311, all finish in frame phase 5 (FUN_0051df30), so the bit is set and slot +0x220 FUN_00511300 fires before the computer player's phase-8 round; the AI's Move only queues and runs at the next step, when the bit clears. The port evaluated the rule after the AI's orders, so a fleet sent on its arrival day never blockaded. Fix: BlockadeSystem::advance now runs after arrivals, battles and landings and before the AI round, in simulation.rs and the native loop in main.rs; running regiments still roll at the blockade step. telemetry_coverage: blockade 30 events; only repair is missing. Golden unchanged (2/2). Also corrected: the system vtable is 0x0065e640 (FUN_00507130), so FUN_00508660 is slot +0xc8, reached from event 0x301's FUN_00514510 (blockade-troop-withdrawal.md, blockade.rs comment).
Native e2e after the Death Star fix (2026-10-15, Alliance player, seed 42, .artifacts/native-checks/2026-10-15-ds-alliance2 on the Mini): days 30/60/90/120 List systems show the Empire AI holding 6 fleets and 10 squadrons at Coruscant, Denab growing 5 to 6 squadrons; no Empire fleet leaves Coruscant by day 120. The original in the VM (alliance-day54-advice.sav run to day 429) also launched no Empire fleet attack.
Original (VM, alliance-day54-advice.sav run on at Slow/Medium): the Empire's first fleet attack is a Battle Alert on day 493, Fleet 7 (Star Destroyer Tyrant, two TIE Fighter squadrons) threatening Alliance-held Praesitlyn, met by the Alliance's Fleet 2 (one Bulk Cruiser). Captures: .artifacts/vm/empire-ai-2026-10-15/day493-*.png. Port, seed 42 native Alliance game: no Empire fleet leaves Coruscant through day 120.
close_reason: Manufacturing and blockade emit: the original production modules (ai_production.rs), the original control rule (or-pfrm), the Death Star class node (FUN_004739b0) and the blockade rule running before the AI round (event 0x311 settles in phase 5, blockade-bit.md). telemetry_coverage: blockade 30, manufacturing 1029; repair moves to or-lzz3.

title: Port: regiments of both sides keep the earlier troop side (FUN_0050b610 bits 4-5)
description: FUN_0050b610 leaves the troop-side bits 4-5 unchanged when both sides have regiments at a system, and FUN_005588f0 takes the holder from those bits when set, so the earlier troop side keeps the system; economy.rs resolve_system_control returns ControlKind::Contested instead (a port: tag). For an unpopulated system (+0x88 bit 0 clear) FUN_0050b610 sets the support bits 2-3 to 3 (neutral), but the troop bits still decide; the port returns Uncontrolled before reading regiments. Contested is read by blockade, the UI and the AI, so the change crosses crates: explain before changing. Done when both cases follow the original, verified e2e on both sides.

title: Replace the invented message-log text outside the strike plan
description: Message-log lines in crates/rebellion-app/src/main.rs that carry English text with no TEXTSTRA id or source. Each line should get the original's message (TEXTSTRA id, notification kind) or file nothing. Groups: combat result lines (Space battle at ...); manufacturing and delivery (Construction complete, Unit arrived, Unit lost on arrival, queue idle, maintenance shortfall fallback); regiment and squadron arrival and loss; resources discovered and System revealed; story events, special-force landings, uprising incidents and their TEXTSTRA fallbacks, loyalty fallback; betrayal, Jedi tier, Force discovered; mission dispatch and outcome lines (player and AI); AI fleet moves; research level; fleet arrival fallback; session lines (command, saved, loaded, deleted). Developer palette readouts are out of scope. The strike, assault, bombardment, jail, Death Star, victory and movie lines are already sourced (orbital-strike plan).

title: Native Alliance opening: the day clock stalls during the droids' cockpit briefing with briefing=false
description:
Seed 42, Alliance player, native (--live), 2026-10-16. The day clock stood still from ~9.3 s to ~20.4 s at day 8, Slow, with Status reporting briefing=false and pause_alert=false; it began as the Alliance droids' cockpit briefing ran ('[advisor] cockpit step 2 13 at step 5', nine advice topics filed, the Advice index opened then closed by the dev policy). The same opening held a new game at day 0 for 300 frames. Empire runs show nothing like it. Find what holds the clock (advisor_state.holds_clock? the cockpit step?) and settle against the original's briefing (FUN_00487ff0 hold_speed_for_advice). Found by the scheduler step-4 native checks; does not affect their results.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Start a native `--live` game, seed 42, as the Alliance, at Slow.
2. Let the droids' cockpit briefing run at day 8.
3. Status reports briefing=false and pause_alert=false while the day clock stands still from about 9.3 s to 20.4 s.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] What holds the clock is named and settled against the original's briefing (`FUN_00487ff0`).
- [ ] The day clock behaves as the original's through the briefing, Alliance and Empire.

title: Q: Does the original AI send damaged ships to a shipyard, and should ship records carry damage (FUN_00484630)?
description: telemetry_coverage (crates/rebellion-data/tests/telemetry_coverage.rs, ignored) fails only on repair after or-glv7. Repair emits when a damaged ship sits at a system with a shipyard (repair.rs): six 1500-tick dual-AI playtests (seeds 1-6) log 48, 64 and 74 repair events in seeds 3, 5 and 6, none in 1, 2, 4; seed 2 has two battles whose surviving side was damaged and never repaired; the seed-42 test galaxy has no damaged survivor in 1000 days (every winner keeps full hull). FUN_00484630 scales a ship record's attack and shield figures by the weapons and shields left (obj+0x264/+0x290); the port's ship_record (ai_records.rs) keeps class figures. Trace whether any AI module (8, 9, 12, 13) or the record need bits route a damaged ship or fleet to a yard, port it if so, then rerun telemetry_coverage. Do not change the test's expectation without that evidence.
notes: Answered (ghidra/notes/ship-damage-repair.md, 17 new .c files): yes, module 11 phase 0x3f8 step 2 FUN_004c8e90 moves mobile damaged ships to the nearest own unblockaded shipyard-role system, and FUN_00484630 scales the ship record by six damage counters (ship+0x64); repair runs everywhere every 30 days, every 2 at an own counted shipyard. Port work: or-39er.
close_reason: Answered from the decompiles; the port moves to or-39er (damage counters, FUN_004c8e90, repair cadence).

title: Q: Does the original resolve every battle of a day before the day moves on, and the AI order again?
description: Native port (scheduler step 4): the combat loop opens one player battle per tick and leaves the other contested systems for the next tick's combat stage (held_battles); AI orders touching them are recorded 'held' and the module resets (settle(false)), so module 8 re-issues the same Reinforce move about every second round: ~300 held ai_action records in one Very Slow day (seed 42, Alliance player, battles staged at Coruscant and Ghorman). held orders are uncounted, so the cap is unaffected. The original shows Battle Alerts in sequence while the day stands still (FUN_0040a050 states 5-0x17; save alliance-day54, Praesitlyn days 508/532), which suggests all of a day's battles resolve before the next round. Settle in the VM with two battles due the same day: does the second alert open before the day advances? If so, port it (open the remaining battles before the clock resumes) and drop the next-tick deferral; the held flood goes with it. Until then, no damping.

title: Port: per-side views for the AI system record (FUN_0050fc80, FUN_0050d5a0)
description:
The AI system record (`ai_records::fill_system`, `FUN_00433e40.c:120-125`) stops at Q `0x80` when the side's view of the system lacks `+0x88` bit 1. `FUN_0050fc80` copies that bit, with bit 0 (populated, `FUN_0050fbf0`), into a side's view while the view is live, and an observation level refresh (`FUN_0050d5a0`: informants, espionage, mission ends) copies it too; a view that stops being live keeps the bit (`ghidra/notes/observation-levels.md`).

The port has no per-side views. `fill_system` reads the bit as held for a core system (SYSTEMSD family `0x90`), a system the side holds, and one where it has a usable fleet (`hyp:` in its doc). It misses a view kept from an earlier observation and every observation-level refresh. The world's `exploration_status` cannot stand in: either side's intelligence mission sets it (integrator `SystemIntelligenceGathered`), which leaked the other side's espionage into this side's record.

Port: keep per side which systems' views hold bit 1 (set when the view goes live and on each `FUN_0050d5a0` refresh, never cleared) and have `fill_system` read the side's own. Save-format change (SAVE_VERSION bump). Both factions.

Done when: `fill_system` reads the per-side view state with the citations above, its `hyp:` is gone, tests cover a kept view and an espionage refresh for either side, and the seed-42 golden is regenerated for this named cause.

title: Ship picks in the 3D view follow each tactical mode's +0xc
description:
## Background

`ghidra/notes/tactical-selection-modes.md` ("The 3D view", "Ship picks by mode") traces what a ship pick in the 3D view does in each tactical mode: the current mode's `+0xc(id, Ctrl)` decides. In mode `0xe` (one own capital) a plain click on another own ship escorts it when `FUN_005ae260` allows (`FUN_005a1af0.c:65-101`), an enemy becomes the sole target (`:167-171`) and Ctrl adds or removes targets (`:187-219`). In `0x10` a plain own-ship click forms a task force in the first free slot that escorts it (`FUN_005a24d0.c:55-71`), and an enemy forms one with that target (`:180-191`). In a task-force mode a member clicked with Ctrl leaves the task force, and the last member also clears the slot and returns to the base mode (`FUN_005a3aa0.c:116-137`); a plain member click makes the other members a new task force that escorts it (`:53-72`). A right click reaches the same `+0xc` (`FUN_005c2060.c:136-169`).

The port's `pick_own_ship` (`crates/rebellion-render/src/tactical_view.rs`) covers the plain pick (one ship selected, no strip pressed), Ctrl multi-selection, and a Ctrl+click that moves a non-member into the selected task force. A plain click on an own ship always reselects it, and Ctrl+click on a member only toggles its selection, because every port ship carries a task-force index (`TacticalShip::task_force`), so a ship cannot leave a task force for a group of its own (`FUN_005aded0`).

## Scope

Ship picks in the 3D view follow the traced `+0xc` of modes `0xe`, `0x10` and 1-8 for own ships, both buttons, with and without Ctrl, both sides. That needs a ship state outside every task-force slot (the original's own group), which the strip, the HUD and the focus rules must then read.

## Tests

One behaviour test per traced row of "Ship picks by mode", citing its lines, red first; `cargo mutants` on the touched functions.

## E2E

A native run on each side: select a task force, Ctrl+click a member out of it, Ctrl+click the last member (the slot clears); a two-ship selection clicked on an own ship forms a task force in the first free slot.

## Evidence

Seed, system and day; the `[tactical_groups]` lines; captures of the strip after each step.

## Constraints

AGENTS.md applies: both factions, cited original behaviour, red-first tests in a Mini clone, Mini-only cargo, silent runs, the browser only through the interface-parity gates, no commit before Tom's word.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] A ship can stand outside every task-force slot, and Ctrl+click on a member of the selected task force moves it out (FUN_005a3aa0.c:116-137); the last member's leaving clears the slot and returns to the base mode, both sides
- [ ] A plain own-ship pick in modes 0xe, 0x10 and 1-8 does what FUN_005a1af0, FUN_005a24d0 and FUN_005a3aa0 trace (escort, a new task force in the first free slot, or a new task force of the other members), both sides
- [ ] Enemy picks in 0xe and 0x10 set targets or form a task force as FUN_005a1af0.c:134-219 and FUN_005a24d0.c:143-191 trace
- [ ] The named tests are green after being shown red, and the scoped mutants are killed or explained
- [ ] A native run on each side shows the E2E steps in captures and [tactical_groups] lines

title: Port: Withdraw gives each capital ship a group of its own (FUN_005ad530, FUN_005aded0)
description:
## Background

Withdraw (`FUN_005ad530`, from command `0x7a` and the computer controller) regroups the withdrawing side before it orders it out. For each capital ship of the side (list `+0x58`, `FUN_005ad530.c:61-81`):
- a ship whose task force holds a strip slot of the local side empties that slot (`FUN_005a0c50`, `FUN_005a0410`);
- the ship leaves its group (`FUN_005a8d30`);
- `FUN_005aded0` gives it a group of its own (`FUN_005ade20` out of the old one, `FUN_005cbf50` new, `+0x178` set, `FUN_005aded0.c:21-37`);
- that group takes order 3, Withdraw.

The Withdraw executor's front-ship rule (`FUN_005cc300.c:77-145`) then applies to one-ship groups, so each capital ship jumps when it can, not one per old task force. Both sides branch nowhere here. ghidra/notes/morale-retreat.md, "Windowed withdrawal"; ghidra/notes/tactical-group-strips.md, Port.

## Scope

`crates/rebellion-core/src/tactical.rs`: `begin_side_withdrawal` gives each of the side's capital ships a group of its own; `advance_withdraw_orders` keeps its front-ship rule over those groups. The port's `TacticalShip::task_force` is a slot index 0-7 and is read by targeting, formation and the strips, so the regroup needs a representation for a group outside the eight slots. The strips already read a withdrawn side as having no task force (`in_player_task_force`, `fighter_group_slot_held`). Out of scope: the computer side's choice to withdraw.

## Design

Options: a per-ship withdrawal group id beside `task_force`; or a `task_force` value outside 0-7 for "own group". Pick by what targeting (`FUN_005a24d0`), formation and the status panel read; the status panel's selected-ship art reads the selected ships' task force today.

## Tests

- `a_withdrawing_side_jumps_each_capital_ship_on_its_own`, citing `FUN_005ad530.c:61-81` and `FUN_005aded0.c:21-37`, both sides; red first in a Mini clone.
- `a_task_force_jumps_one_ship_at_a_time` (withdrawal_tests.rs) cites `FUN_005cc300.c:84-101` but builds a two-ship task force that Withdraw would have split; its expectation changes for that cited cause.
- `cargo mutants` on the touched functions; the replay golden rerun.

## E2E

Native, both factions: a battle with a two-ship task force, Withdraw, countdown out; both ships jump without waiting on each other (`[tactical_withdrawal]` and jump log lines).

## Evidence

The jump log lines' times for each ship, by save, day and battle.

## Constraints

AGENTS.md applies.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] begin_side_withdrawal puts each of the side's capital ships in a group of its own, citing FUN_005ad530.c:61-81 and FUN_005aded0.c:21-37, both sides.
- [ ] Each withdrawing capital ship jumps without waiting on its old task force's front ship, shown by a red-first test.
- [ ] A native run on each side shows two ships of one task force jumping independently after Withdraw.

title: Q: How does a system change sides in the original, and what does FUN_0050b610 compute?
description: economy.rs resolve_system_control reads FUN_0050b610 as the control rule (troops of one side only -> that side controls; none and low energy -> uncontrolled). The decompile (ghidra/notes/FUN_0050b610.c) builds a 2-bit field (local_30 >> 4 & 3) from the two sides' regiment queries (FUN_00504cc0 side 1 and 2, FUN_005131b0) and nothing in it writes control. In the port no diplomacy success ever makes a neutral system join a side: a 400-day dual-AI playtest (seed 42) ends with Alliance 2 systems, Empire 3, neutral 95, as a run from before the AI port did; 195 Diplomacy missions, several successes, one control change (Drall to Uncontrolled); on day 1 Corellia, Vagran and Xyquine drop to Uncontrolled. The stalled economy starves the AI: the Alliance's maintenance capacity stays 100 (load 87), module 6's facility budget is 4 against a training facility's 10, so it never builds one and never trains a regiment, and module 8's postures never get the regiment surplus their assault and drop targets need. Settle in the original (VM): what makes a neutral system join a side (support threshold? GNPRTB?), and what the FUN_0050b610 field feeds. Game-rule code: explain before changing. Done when the port follows the original for both sides, verified e2e.
notes:
2026-10-15: now also blocks or-glv7: with the original AI ported, the starved economy leaves both sides without a fleet to attack (no Move of a fleet, no battle in 1000 days). Settling this rule is the next step for the AI's e2e.
2026-10-15 decompile reading: FUN_0050b610 rebuilds the system control word (+0x84, validated by FUN_00558880). Bits 2-3, the support side: 3 when +0x88 bit 0 (populated) is clear, else FUN_0055a080(sys+0x58) = 1 when Alliance support >= DAT_006bb4c0, 2 when 100 - support >= it, else 3 (neutral). DAT_006bb4c0 is GNPRTB 0x1e50 = 7760 (60), loaded in FUN_00558bb0. Bits 4-5, the troop side (FUN_00504cc0 regiment queries per side, FUN_005131b0): 1 Alliance only, 2 Empire only, unchanged when both, 0 when none. The holder (bits 0-1, FUN_005588f0) is the troop side when bits 4-5 are set, else the support side; FUN_0050a300 commits it. So a system without troops belongs to the side whose support reaches 60, neutral between 41 and 59. The port's resolve_system_control compares total_energy with GNPRTB 7760 instead, and with no troops keeps or clears control; that is why no system ever joins a side.
2026-10-15: ported. economy.rs resolve_system_control: no regiments -> FUN_0055a080 on the Alliance support (sys+0x58) against GNPRTB 7760 (60): >=60 Alliance, 100-support >=60 Empire, else neutral. Two economy tests rewritten (support 60/40 both ways, 50 neutral); two rebellion-data simulation fixtures gained GNPRTB 7760 (GameConfig::default has no table, so the threshold read 0) and holder-side support. Golden regenerated (cause: the original control rule): v1:5499c2812292dc6a -> v1:e4e12a02bb66d9cd, 3/3. 1000-day dual-AI playtest: control 8/8/84 (was 2/3/95), 2 attack orders, 2 space battles, 2 bombardments; telemetry_coverage now has combat, still misses blockade and repair (repair missing before the new AI too). Port gaps kept: unpopulated -> neutral; both troops -> contested (original keeps the earlier troop side). Native check pending.
close_reason: Ported FUN_0050b610's no-regiment rule (FUN_0055a080 on support vs GNPRTB 7760). Playtest control 2/3/95 -> 8/8/84 with battles and bombardments; native seed 42 holders steady day 0->2 playing either side (.artifacts/native-checks/2026-10-15-pfrm-alliance, -empire). Golden regenerated for the cause. Remaining both-troops and unpopulated cases: or-i7uo.

title: Port: the AI's Abort order 0x250
description:
## Background

The AI's planners issue order `0x250` (Abort) from `FUN_0047b250`, which
aborts the planner's mission while the mission is in state 8
(`FUN_00520b30`) and the planner's flags carry `0x20000000`, or `0x40000000`
when the planner's slot `+0x34` returns 0
(`ghidra/notes/ai-order-emission.md`, the order table and "Abort").
Registry-B command `0x250` is a different thing that shares the id getter
(`ghidra/notes/ai-mission-planning.md`). The port emits every other planner
order but not Abort; what slot `+0x34` returns is still open in the note.

## Scope

`crates/rebellion-core/src/mission_planning.rs` (the planners) and
`missions.rs` (the phase that waits for timer `0x38b`, `FUN_00520b30`), plus
the integrator path that applies an abort. Out: the HQ
Move (`or-alliance-hq-move-o9ms`) and Rename `0x203` (`or-9ia9`).

## Tests

Behaviour-sentence tests for both sides, citing `FUN_0047b250` and
`FUN_00520b30`: a planner whose mission sits in state 8 with the flag set
issues Abort and the mission ends; without the flag it does not. Red first
in a Mini clone; `cargo mutants` on the touched functions.

## E2E

A seeded headless playtest or native dev-command run in which a planner's
mission reaches state 8, both sides, with the Abort visible in the AI trace.

## Constraints

AGENTS.md applies. Settle slot `+0x34` from the trace before porting the
`0x40000000` branch; if it needs its own question, file it as
`discovered-from` this bead.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] What the planner's slot +0x34 returns is settled from the trace and cited.
- [ ] A planner whose mission is in state 8 with flag 0x20000000 (or 0x40000000 when slot +0x34 returns 0) issues Abort and the mission ends, for both sides (FUN_0047b250, FUN_00520b30).
- [ ] Its tests failed first in a Mini clone, and the touched functions' mutants are caught or explained.
- [ ] A seeded run shows the Abort in the AI trace for each side.

description:

title: Port: a lost ship's characters go adrift and take the wound roll, never captive
description:
## Background

When a capital ship is destroyed in a space battle (reason `0xc`,
`FUN_0040cfc0.c:88`), its hook `FUN_00502840` walks every child: a
character's slot `+0xb4` is `FUN_004ef2e0`, which sets the Adrift role
(`FUN_00534790(1)`, event `0x30e`) and never captures. With the reason in
1..`0x10`, each character aboard and not in transit first takes the wound
roll (`FUN_004ef640` -> `FUN_0053ea00`, GNPRTB `0xa08`-`0xa0a`); a minor then
dies on the `G2577` roll (`0xa11`), a major is only wounded
(`ghidra/notes/tactical-results.md`, "The lost ship's characters (read)").

The port captures them instead: `post_battle::destroy_fleet` marks every
character aboard captive of the winner (`crates/rebellion-core/src/post_battle.rs`,
the loop after `let captor = side(!is_alliance)`), a `hyp:` that cites
`or-q-emptied-fleet-crew-iz3z`.

## Scope

`crates/rebellion-core/src/post_battle.rs` (`destroy_fleet`) and the
character state it touches. The adrift sweep and the Destroy System cascade
stay as they are. The VM settle of the question stays on
`or-q-emptied-fleet-crew-iz3z`.

## Tests

Behaviour-sentence tests for both sides, citing `FUN_004ef2e0` and
`FUN_004ef640`: a major aboard a lost ship ends adrift and wounded, not
captive; a minor dies or ends adrift by the rolls. Shown red against the
current capture first, in a Mini clone; `cargo mutants` on `destroy_fleet`.

## E2E

A native `Battle at` run on the Mini (`agent_docs/dev-commands.md`) for each
side with a character aboard a ship that dies; the readout shows the
character adrift, not captive.

## Constraints

AGENTS.md applies. The `hyp:` tag is replaced by the citations above.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] A major aboard a destroyed ship ends adrift and wounded, not captive, for both sides (FUN_004ef2e0, FUN_004ef640).
- [ ] A minor aboard takes the wound roll and dies on the G2577 roll or ends adrift, for both sides.
- [ ] The hyp: in post_battle::destroy_fleet is replaced by these citations, and its tests failed first in a Mini clone.
- [ ] A native Battle at run per side shows the character adrift after its ship dies.

title: Port: a load reopens the saved strategic windows
description: The original saves the strategic view's child windows as the save's third section (writer FUN_00440ea0, reader FUN_00440f80 → FUN_00441190), bottom of the z-order to top: a six-word descriptor (type, x, y, w, h, shown) plus a per-type payload for Sector (1), Fleet (4, with tab), Battle in Progress (7), System (9), Defenses (10) and Missions (11). The GID mode is replayed through WM_COMMAND 0x140. Shown windows come back shown, hidden ones on the minimized rail, and sector windows drop to the bottom; restored windows open silently. System, Defenses and Missions pages are not saved; System reopens on Overview. The port saves no interface state and closes every window on a load; the GID category is neither saved nor reset. Port plan: an InterfaceState save section outside the state fingerprint (fleet windows by FleetKey, which the save keeps stable with the slotmap versions), per-family export/restore, and main.rs wiring after the GID focus model.
notes:
Wine checks (Empire day-2 start, played on to day 6 / day 8): a dragged System window reopens where it was dragged (322,92), so the descriptor's x and y follow a drag; a System window saved on Shipyards reopens on the Manufacturing overview; a window minimized to the rail comes back on the rail; the sector window comes back under the System window. Saved with the GID menu open: the menu does not reopen; a System window the menu had hidden comes back on the rail (GID's slot +0x08 clears +0x110, so it saves as hidden); a sector window the menu had hidden comes back shown, because FUN_00441190's type-1 branch clears its rail flag (0x441248 jumps to 0x4413f1, as type 7 does), so only +0x2c(5) follows; the legend category was unchanged (Popular Support), so the GID-mode replay is not exercised. The Fleet window's subject is its system (fleet-window.md, +0x144), as the port keys it, so fleet windows save by system DatId; no FleetKey is needed. The Battle in Progress overlay (type 7) is left out: the port has no such window. The record types live in rebellion_core::saved_interface; they follow SaveState in the body, outside the fingerprint, under the save version current when this lands.
2026-10-20: native, both sides, release build, muted, seed 42. Empire: a Fleet window over a System window comes back in front with the keyboard after save and load; Escape closes the Fleet window, then the System window. Alliance: the Yavin Fleet window over Ghorman's System window comes back on top, same Escape order. Open: a browser save and load on both sides that asserts the restored windows (positions, the rail, the System page, the GID mode, the focus); wasm32 save_slot_with_interface and load_slot_with_interface have no gate and their two mutants were accepted on this check. Optional: a Wine save with a non-default GID category to observe the 0x140 replay.
2026-10-20: browser, both sides, production build, Chrome with --mute-audio --disable-audio-output (Firefox and Safari parity is not claimed): window-restore.mjs 2 of 2. Empire seed 42 day 9 and Alliance seed 3 day 60: a dragged System window on Shipyards, a second System window on the rail, a Fleet window dragged over the first and Uprisings (Alt+2), saved to Game Options row 2 and loaded from the main menu in a fresh page, come back pixel for pixel: Fleet window in front, System window at its dragged place on Overview, rail slot 1 as saved, the Uprisings map. Escape closes the Fleet window, then the System window; a third Escape leaves the rail. A Fleet window saves unless SystemWindowState::rail_holds_fleet holds it, whatever the frame paints, since Game Options suspends the strategic scene (FUN_00440ea0 walks the view's child windows). Tests: a_save_from_game_options_keeps_a_shown_fleet_window_shown_and_a_minimized_one_hidden (both sides) and the_rail_holds_a_minimized_fleet_window_and_no_other_for_either_side. A restored window is clamped into the galaxy view while a drag is not: or-q-restored-window-clamp-wqt5.
close_reason: Done: native and browser restore on both sides

title: Q: Where do the AI's Destroy System inputs come from, and does the AI ever build or fire the Death Star?
description: ghidra/notes/death-star-strategic.md, AI: the posture emitter FUN_004b1070 issues 0x223 when the fleet record flag +0x38 & 0x10 (from object +0x50 bit 7 via FUN_00433780) and the target record +0x110 are set; trace +0x110's writers (FUN_004739b0 and the census) and whether the AI class flag 0x200000 (FUN_0042e960, FUN_0041b230) admits CAPSHPSD record 136. Also the refusal a second family-0x18 ship at one system raises (FUN_00550bd0, FUN_0054fd90) and what clears a destroyed system's populated bit (FUN_0050b760, FUN_0050a3c0, FUN_00508660).
notes:
2026-10-18: the module-11 budget is read (FUN_004ca5e0): the hull needs capacity 2223, and the module's budget is 0.27 x capacity - c+0x24c. Measured 2026-10-17 on the release playtest (dual AI, standard galaxy, medium difficulty, seeds 1-24): no Death Star build, no DestroySystem order and no death_star_fired in 1,500 or 5,000 days, and no game ended by victory. Capacity is not the gate (the Empire reaches 2,223 by day 1,500 in 17 seeds); the fielded capital-ship maintenance c+0x24c is, with budget median 35 at day 1,500, 15 at 3,000, 13 at 5,000. Of 240 samples three reach 600 (seeds 22, 7, 4), and the class is listed in all 240. Around seed 22's day 2,000 module 11 builds capital-ship keys 17 and 18 instead, so an earlier row of FUN_004ca5e0 holds the turn (hyp: which row is not traced). The budget mismatch is ported; no seed issues 0x223 yet.
2026-10-18 (module 11's turn): the request rows run in a fixed order (FUN_004ca5e0.c:57-139) and a blocker lasts one request (FUN_004ca910.c:26 clears all, :67-68 sets only the failed row's), so a row whose class fits runs every pass. The troop-room row (rec+0x64 bit 4, R+0x74 < 0 after FUN_00477e80's takers) comes first and wins whenever one record holds the bit; its cheap transport classes (mask 0x100004, key 0x100) always fit, so the hull row (eighth) is never reached. The port's request and pick match the code (ai_production.rs ship_request, capital_ships). Measured on the port's seed 22 (dual AI, release playtest, trace in a private copy): the Empire's budget clears 600 from day 1,594 (603 to 872 by day 1,800); every request to day 1,904 takes the troop-room row with blockers 0 and builds class key 28 (maintenance 20), 41 transports between days 1,300 and 1,700, while fielded capital-ship maintenance falls from 736 (day 1,100) to 430 (day 1,552) and a record stays troop-short. No port change, so the 24-seed census needs no re-measure; the strict fleet rule did not touch the census inputs. Remaining scope: (1) why a record stays short of troop room while transports are built and lost: the takers of FUN_00477e80 (take_free, poach) and the troop-room counter of FUN_00477cb0 against the original, and where the transports go; (2) the 0x223 seed test with a ready hull fleet at an HQ system with regiments loaded.
2026-10-18 (troop-room stall, item 1): line-by-line against the decompiles, no deviation. FUN_00477cb0's counters (troop room = fleet +0x84 sum) match sum_and_require; FUN_00477e80's short set, need bits and let-go test match shortfall_and_surplus; the kind-6 requirement FUN_004b6a60 (P+0x3c rises to the larger of sector +0x134 and c+0x170, never falls while the posture lasts) matches requirement(); take_free matches FUN_004782a0 (nearest fleets with 0x8005, ships with 0x20000 and none of 0xc03800, serving a shortfall); poach matches FUN_00478690 (0x8001, none of 0xf0000006, later plan entry, ships none of 0xc23800); repair_move matches FUN_004c8e90 except the port's hyp that a Move to the fleet's own system is not issued (the original issues 0x201 whenever the pick is a system). Seed 22 trace (private copy): the short record is kind 6 at Sumitra, troop room 3-5 below 18 from day 1,275; take_free finds nothing each pass because every free transport is en route (0x800) or damaged (0x1000); transports 13 and 47 stay free and damaged from day 1,425 and keep changing systems (Bortras, Coruscant, Yaga Minor); the Empire issues one repair move in the run (day 1,609, Bothawui to Orto); Empire fleet moves in that window (fleet 28v5, days 1,476 and 1,481) carry no AI order (hyp: post-battle retreats, unchecked). No port change, so no re-measure. Whether the original escapes the stall on a comparable game is a game-state question the code cannot settle; it needs an original-game observation (an Empire AI game soaked under Wine to the day its troop records go short). Remaining: the repair_move own-system hyp (minor), and that observation.

title: Q: Does the original's battle end with the loser destroyed, or does a losing side withdraw and survive?
description: In the port every battle runs to the end (simulate_to_end): in 15 headless passes over 1000 days of seeds 1-12, 7 and 42, and in four native alert-resolved battles (Hoth, Yavin; 2026-10-16-postbattle-empire2), the loser had no fleet or squadron left, so the post-battle relocation chain (FUN_00516ef0, event 0x307, FUN_00515480) never ran. Two passes took their winner from the holder rule (seed 8 tick 237 Corfai, seed 11 tick 383 Averam) but with one side gone, so no pass followed. Question: in the original, does auto-resolve or the tactical AI withdraw a losing side (ships surviving at the system or leaving), and when? Settle in the VM (vm-game.sh resolve on a Battle Alert; compare the forces before and after) and in the tactical AI's withdraw decision. Needed to stage the surviving-loser and holder-tie e2e checks of the post-battle pass.
notes:
2026-10-16 VM (empire-day30-yaga-alert-control.sav, .artifacts/vm/loser-2026-10-16): Battle at Yaga Minor, Alliance Fleet 3 (Bulk Cruiser 3, the AI's) against Imperial Fleet 1 (ISD 1, TIE squadrons). Auto-resolve: 'The Imperial fleet is victorious. Imperial forces have maintained the blockade of Yaga Minor. The Alliance fleet has withdrawn.' Results, Alliance capital ships: Bulk Cruiser 3 Operational, No Casualties. So the original's loser survives and withdraws; the port's simulate_to_end destroys it. Next: find the original's withdraw decision (the AI side's retreat at the alert, or auto-resolve's withdrawal) in the decompiles.
Port, seeds 1-20 x 1000 days --dual-ai --trace combat: 222 battles; 220 decisive with the loser left with no capital ship and no squadron, 2 draws with neither side left (seed 8 tick 237 Corfai, seed 11 tick 383 Averam); 0 post-battle relocations.
Answered (ghidra/notes/morale-retreat.md): the tactical engine's per-second morale check FUN_005d19a0 (called from FUN_005d14d0:101 after the side's damage) withdraws a side whose strength (FUN_005d0ce0) is 0 or below threshold*enemy (side +0x24), when retreat is permitted (+0x80: a retreat system exists, FUN_00516730; no opposing gravity-well ship, hyp; working hyperdrive). Threshold: computer 0.9 by default, min(own/enemy fleet attack, 0.9) at its own system with its squadrons, 0 at its HQ (FUN_004e6110); human 0. Yaga Minor: Alliance computer threshold 0.9, so Bulk Cruiser 3 jumps in the first second, after shields absorb the Empire's first volley. The port never runs the check. Open: whether played battles run it, the reader of +0x7c.
Port landed (uncommitted): BattleSession::morale (threshold, retreat_permitted, retreated, gravity_wells), BattleSession::morale_withdraws run in headless_step after each side's damage, Empire side first (FUN_005ae9c0:26-27); apply::seat_morale seats permission (post_battle::retreat_destination, port: for FUN_00516730) and threshold (ai_records::battle_withdraw_threshold, FUN_004e6110; human side 0.0). Played (windowed) step does not run the check; Death Star, squadron hyperdrive and side +0x7c delay not modeled.
2026-10-16 native, morale port (release build): Empire run .artifacts/native-checks/2026-10-16-morale-empire3: Hoth day 1 'The Imperial fleet is victorious. Hoth has been cleared of Alliance forces. The Alliance fleet has withdrawn.' (departed=yes to Storthus); Yavin day 7 'Yavin is now under blockade by Imperial forces. The Alliance fleet has withdrawn.' (departed=yes). (departed=yes). The loser withdraws and survives on both sides, as in the original (VM, Yaga Minor). Controller request FUN_004e8290: add while tree bit clear and count<capable; drop (oldest unflagged, hyp: slot +0x18 untraced) when count>capable or tree done and count>0.
